focus.product: Essential-oil distillers and small agro-processing machines
focus.why: Essential oils and fish processing are Aceh's official industri unggulan (Permenperin 130/2010). PT Sang General Industri (Aceh Besar) already holds TKDN 34-40% for SS304 essential-oil distillers, cocoa and threshing machines. Aceh's registered metal base is tiny (SIINas: 10 metal and machinery firms), so a fabrication-plus-CNC machinery niche is the realistic start. National imports 2025: 841940 not retrieved (Comtrade quota, 16 Oct 2026).

also.product: Fishing-boat propellers, shafts and stern gear
also.why: Fish and seafood processing is Aceh's other official priority (Permenperin 130/2010). The nearest certified propeller maker is in Asahan, Sumatera Utara (TKDN 72.74-83.41%). 3D-printed patterns plus CNC finishing suit small batches. National imports 2025: 848710 not retrieved (Comtrade quota, 16 Oct 2026).

also.product: Maintenance spares for KEK Arun Lhokseumawe gas, fertiliser and petrochemical plants (pump, valve and compressor parts)
also.why: KEK Arun (PP 5/2017) targets energy, petrochemicals, agro-industry, logistics and kraft paper; PIM runs urea (570,000 t/yr), ammonia and NPK plants; PT Wira Cipta Perkasa (Aceh Utara) packages gas compressors. National imports 2025: 841391 US$300.0M; 848190 US$185.7M.

The local metal base is thin (SIINas: 26 metal and machinery firms, no foundry), so this needs a foundry-plus-CNC build-up.

focus.product: Maintenance spares for steel and petrochemical plants: rolling-mill rolls and roll-shop work, pump impellers and shafts, valve and heat-exchanger parts (reverse-engineered)
focus.why: The Krakatau Steel group and Krakatau Posco make slab, plate, HRC, CRC and pipe here. Chandra Asri (polyethylene), Asahimas (VCM/PVC) and coal power plants form the region's heavy-process base, and all of them consume wear and rotating parts. Indonesia imported US$34.9M of rolls (8455.30) and US$68.4M of rolling-mill parts (8455.90) in 2024, plus US$296.6M of pump parts (8413.91). Fabricators already exist (Daekyung Indah in KIEC, Tuban Steel Work, Timas Suplindo). Politeknik Industri Petrokimia Banten trains machine technicians.

also.product: Gas valves and valve parts: LPG cylinder valves and forged or brass valve bodies
also.why: PT Asa Bintang Pratama (Modern Cikande) holds TKDN of 92.20-97.86% for LPG cylinder valves. This is a fully localised, high-content product line that can be scaled up.

focus.product: Forged blades and hand tools finished on CNC and laser (golok/machetes, knives, hoes, sickles)
focus.why: The densest metal-working base in the unit is blades: Garut has 536 small units making cutting and hand tools (223 for carpentry, 313 household; provincial RPIP data cited in Garut RPIK 2021, pre-2023) and Kab. Tasikmalaya 323 golok units with 1,664 workers and Rp124.8bn yearly output (2018 data; Manonjaya incl. Galonggong, Cikatomas, Singaparna). Ciamis adds Kampung Dokdak (Baregbeg), with about 30 toolmaker groups making knives, machetes, golok, hoes and axes for Tasikmalaya, Banjar, Pangandaran and Bandung; a 2024 university programme gave them belt grinders and blowers. Smiths mostly work by hand and lose to factory and Chinese tools (Garut 2019, Pangandaran 2021). CNC/laser blanking, CNC grinding and fixtured heat treatment would standardise blades. Kab. Tasikmalaya's plan lists basic metals and capital goods/components as leading industries, zones golok making in Manonjaya, Cikatomas and Singaparna, and notes iron sand and iron ore on its south coast. Trade check (2025): imports of hoes, machetes and other farm hand tools (820130/820140/820190) were under US$0.3M, fixed-blade knives (821192) US$3.1M (75% China), and exports were near zero. The case is upgrading a large domestic cluster and building exports, not import substitution.

focus.product: CNC-cut and bent metal frames, components and weaving jigs for rattan, synthetic-rattan and aluminium furniture
focus.why: Furniture is the unit's largest existing manufacturing base: Kab. Cirebon exported US$66.6M of rattan furniture in 2022 (24.9% of its non-oil exports; aluminium furniture also listed) and rattan furniture/crafts counted 1,520 firms and 65,696 workers in 2023 (plus 1,441 wood-furniture firms). The Kab. Cirebon industry plan (Perda 1/2026) names rattan/wood furniture a leading industry, and the Rebana plan lists furniture for KPI Cirebon and the Tegalwangi (Weru) small-industry centre. Asmindo Cirebon wants output near '70% machine accuracy' (Oct 2024), and the provincial rattan service unit in Cirebon (9,000 m2, shared machines) is a ready host for common CNC equipment. Nationally, Indonesia exported US$98.8M of metal-framed seats (940179) and US$70.2M of other metal furniture (940320) in 2025, against US$19.7M of rattan furniture (940383), so metal frames are where furniture export value sits. Frames, brackets and forming jigs suit CNC laser/plasma cutting, tube bending and routing; 3D printing suits design prototypes. Inference: no Cirebon CNC supplier was verified.

focus.product: Finish-machined iron castings for water and fire networks: valves, hydrant pillars and bodies, flanged pipe fittings and pump housings (Ceper foundry cluster)
focus.why: Kemenperin calls Ceper one of Indonesia's largest foundry centres (260 firms, 3,500 workers in 2016; Koperasi Batur Jaya had 168 members and >4,000 workers in 2019). On 16 Oct 2026, 27 firms in Kecamatan Ceper held TKDN certificates, among them gate valves and hydrant pillars (PT Baja Kurnia), flanges and dismantling joints ND50-1200 (PT Atmaja Jaya), pipe fittings (PT Aneka Adhilogam Karya), pump castings (CV Samudera Steel) and 130-200 mm crank arms and bearing housings (CV Aneka Metal Industri). Klaten's 2021-2041 industry plan names iron and steel foundry in Ceper and Jatinom as a leading industry. In 2025 Indonesia imported US$945M of valves (848180, 54% from China) and US$300M of pump parts (841391), while already exporting more cast pipe fittings (730719, US$34.3M) than it imported (US$5.7M). CNC turning and boring turns rough castings into higher-value finished parts; 3D-printed sand-mould patterns would ease the cluster's pattern-maker shortage.

also.product: Rail and engine wear parts: railway brake blocks and brake parts, cylinder sleeves and liners
also.why: Koperasi Batur Jaya supplied metallic brake blocks to PT KAI for 27 years (to 2019) and shipped 200 cylinder sleeves to a TMMIN supplier in Jan 2019. Railway-parts imports (8607) rose to US$182.4M in 2025 from US$70.7M in 2023; railway air-brake parts (860721) alone rose to US$20.3M from US$6.5M in 2024.

also.product: Maintenance spare parts for sugar and textile mills: shafts, bearing housings, gears and rollers
also.why: PT SGN plans to restart the dormant PG Tasikmadu (Karanganyar) in 2027 with modernised technology. Textiles are a leading industry in the Surakarta, Sukoharjo and Klaten plans. Ceper firms already hold TKDN certificates for large crank arms and bearing housings, and PT ATMI Solo makes precision parts. In 2025 Indonesia imported US$45.8M of food and sugar machinery parts (843890) and US$43M of spinning and weaving machine parts (844839, 844849).

focus.product: CNC-routed furniture components and carved panels for Jepara's furniture exporters
focus.why: Jepara has 387 large exporting carving firms and 3,438 small carving units; carving is about 34.5% of regional GDP (2020 data). In Aug 2026 the Jepara wood-craftsmen association said labour is scarce and the work split is about 50:50 labour to machine, heading for 80% machine. Indonesia exported US$696m of wooden furniture (940360), US$58m of 4420 wood articles and US$34.8m of wooden furniture parts (940391) in 2025.

Indonesia imported US$187.5m of harvesting/threshing machinery (8433) in 2025, 77% from China. It also imported US$10.3m of other threshers (843352) and US$9.5m of agricultural dryers (841934). HS codes are my mapping.

also.product: Juwana brass hardware and fittings (door handles, lamp parts, stove, pump and compressor parts): 3D-printed casting patterns plus CNC finishing
also.why: Juwana has a brass cluster dating to Daendels' era (238 units, 68 registered SMEs, 2009 data). It sand-casts scrap brass with manual lathes, and products are exported (2018 study). Sampurna Brass is among its larger firms. In 2025 Indonesia imported US$63.8m of base-metal building fittings (830241; exports US$15.5m) and US$28.3m of other copper articles (741980). Data are old; HS codes are my mapping.

focus.product: Rolling-stock components: bogie and underframe parts, couplers, brake parts and interior fittings for INKA
focus.why: INKA (Madiun) is the biggest machined-parts buyer in the five units. Its TKDN rose from 33% to 52% (May 2026), it is building KRLs for KAI Commuter and 50 locomotive platforms for UGL Rail (Australia) to 2028, and its in-group supplier IMS runs an 11-ha component plant. Indonesia's rail-parts imports (8607) jumped to US$182.4M in 2025 from $70.7M in 2023 (China 45%, Japan 24%). The 2025 jump came mostly from 'other' rolling-stock parts (860799: US$91.5M, up from $18.9M in 2023), air brakes (860721: $20.3M, from $3.8M), whole bogies (860712: $14.4M) and couplers and buffers (860730: $7.7M); axles, wheels and bogie parts (860719) were $41.3M. Madiun has the region's deepest rail skills (PNM D4 Perkeretaapian, PPI D3 rail mechanics) and a UMK of about 48% of Surabaya's. Other TKDN-certified makers in the unit (2024-25 lists): PT Mitra Maharta (rice-mill chassis and grain-dryer parts, Ponorogo), PT Refindo Intiselaras Indonesia (steel rock bolts, Kota Madiun) and PT Gunung Mas Bersinar (bus bodies, Kab. Madiun).

focus.product: Spare and wear parts for kretek (cigarette) making machines
focus.why: Gudang Garam is headquartered in Kediri. It had about 208 ha of plants across Kediri and Pasuruan (2013) and 21,964 staff at end-2025, and keeps machine maintenance inside its Kediri production directorate, making it the cluster's largest single user of machine parts. Indonesia imported US$35.2M of tobacco-machinery parts (847890) in 2025: 33% from China, 28% Germany, 10% Korea. Polinema's Kediri campus teaches production-and-maintenance engineering, and UMK is 48-63% of Surabaya's. No local maker of these parts was found, so this is a demand-led bet that needs Gudang Garam's vendor approval. Other TKDN-certified metal and vehicle makers in the cluster (2024-26 lists): PT Bintang Kadiri (aluminium, copper and bimetal compression connectors and cable lugs, Kab. Kediri) and PT Multiparts Rakindo and PT Epower Motor Indonesia (three-wheel and electric motorcycles, Jombang).

focus.product: Propellers, propeller shafts and stern fittings for small fishing and trading boats
focus.why: Madura has a long tradition of motorised wooden cargo and fishing boats: leti-leti from Sumenep (about 1,000 in 1979, motorised from the early 1980s), golekan from Telaga Biru and janggolan from Kamal-Sampang. markets.product: Desktop and education 3D printers (FDM) made or assembled locally
markets.local_now: Unknown share. Three local FDM printers hold TKDN certificates (Subsolid XS 40.00%, Haltech H-01 33.40%, AM-22 27.03%; Kemenperin TKDN database, read 16 Oct 2026), plus Politeknik Astra's Innostra 3-in-1 (43% local content, 2023). Volumes are not public. The retail market is led by imported Chinese brands (China 78% of 2025 imports) sold through distributors such as TekLab (Bambu Lab, 2026), AXI (Creality, 2023), Raja 3D and 3D Zaiku.
local_makers: CV Acta Techno Inava, Haltech brand (Sleman)
PT Tridiku Teknokarya Indonesia (city not stated; ITS-linked)
markets.cnc_3d_role: Local makers build frames, plates, hotends and brackets with CNC (aluminium) and 3D printing, and import motion parts and electronics. CNC shops can supply the machined parts.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): 20-40% of public-sector and education units and 5-15% of all units within 3-5 years. Reasoning: Perpres 46/2025 makes government, BUMN and BUMD buyers prioritise products with TKDN above 25%, and local TKDN models exist. Most buyers, though, are private hobbyists and SMEs, who choose Bambu Lab or Creality on price and performance. Value is small: 5-15% of US$2.3M (2025 imports) is about US$0.1-0.35M a year.
certs_needed: INAPROC e-katalog listing for public buyers
markets.jobs_note: No employment data found. Local makers appear to be small firms (CV/PT, university spin-offs). Assembly plus machined-parts supply is a few dozen jobs per maker at most (judgement).

markets.product: Industrial and metal additive-manufacturing machines (powder-bed, DED, binder jet)
markets.local_now: About 0%. No local maker of industrial or metal AM machines was found. 848510 (metal deposit) imports came 99% from China in 2023 and 2025. In 2025, 58,705 kg cost US$2.7M, about US$46 per kg. That is low for metal powder-bed machines, so the line may include non-AM deposition equipment (inference).
markets.cnc_3d_role: Buyers would use these machines for metal parts (implants, tooling inserts, spares) and finish the parts on CNC. The machines themselves are not a realistic local product.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): 0-5% local within 3-5 years. Reasoning: lasers, optics, powder handling and controls are all imported, and annual demand is a few million US$. Indonesia gains more by using the machines (see the implant and tooling segments) than by building them.
markets.jobs_note: None for the machines. Operators and post-processing (CNC, heat treatment) jobs would sit at the users.

markets.product: Clear aligners (3D-printed arch models plus thermoformed trays)
markets.local_now: Unknown share. The Indonesian brand Rata claims '70.000+' patients and '100+ Klinik Rata & partner' in '50+ kota' within 3 years. Its price starts at Rp5.9M, against Rp20M for braces and Rp50M for 'other brands' (rata.id, read 16 Oct 2026). Where Rata's aligners are made is not stated. Zenyum (Singapore, ISO 13485) sells in Indonesia. No aligner appears in the TKDN database (searched 16 Oct 2026). Estimate: 70,000 x Rp5.9M = about Rp413bn cumulative, roughly US$25M at an assumed Rp16,500 per US$. That is a lower bound because prices only 'start from' Rp5.9M.
local_makers: Rata (HQ city not stated; clinics in 50+ cities)
markets.cnc_3d_role: Each treatment stage needs a resin arch model printed by SLA/DLP. PET-G sheet is thermoformed over it, then trimmed by CNC, laser or hand. Direct-printed aligners are emerging. CNC's role is limited to trimming fixtures.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): 50-80% of aligner models for Indonesian patients printed in Indonesia within 3-5 years. Reasoning: models are per-patient, bulky and short-lived, so a local scan-print-thermoform loop beats shipping. The low-price local brand already has national clinic reach. Foreign premium brands may keep producing abroad.
certs_needed: Kemenkes izin edar (AKD for domestic devices)
markets.jobs_note: No data. The work is semi-automated digital lab work (treatment-planning technicians, print and thermoform operators).

markets.product: Dental restorations, models and surgical guides (dental labs)
markets.local_now: Unknown. Finished dental fittings are a small import (US$1.5M in 2025), so most crowns and dentures are presumably made in domestic labs (inference). No dental-lab 3D-printing user was found in sources. UGM's engineering faculty works with its dentistry faculty on dental phantoms and dental 3D printing (UGM, 24 Jun 2025).
markets.cnc_3d_role: CAD/CAM milling (zirconia, PMMA) and resin printing (models, surgical guides, temporary crowns, denture bases) work side by side in a digital dental lab.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): 30-60% of big-city dental-lab model and guide work digital within 5 years. Import substitution is small (US$1.5M). Reasoning: intraoral scanning is spreading with aligners, and printing removes plaster work.
certs_needed: Kemenkes izin edar for dental devices
markets.jobs_note: No data. Digital labs swap plaster and wax technicians for scan, CAD and printer operators.

markets.product: Orthopaedic implants, including patient-specific and porous metal-AM implants
markets.local_now: Unknown. In Dec 2022 Marthys said its one-machine plant limited it to about a 15% market-share target (the only share figure found, older than 2023). TKDN-certified local implants exist: Marthys titanium CMF plate 77.32%, Eka Ormed SS316L implants 43-80%, Risa bone plates 30-40%. Kemenkes said only about 20% of 56,000 registered devices are made domestically (Jun 2025, snippet).
markets.cnc_3d_role: Standard plates, screws and nails are multi-axis and Swiss-type CNC work (Risa cites multi-axis machining of Ti-6Al-4V plus wire EDM). Metal powder-bed AM adds porous acetabular cups, cranio-maxillofacial and patient-specific plates and cutting guides, which are then finished on CNC.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): local makers (all processes) 20-35% of 902110+902131 value within 3-5 years. AM-specific implants 1-3% of segment value, about US$0.5-1.5M a year (0.01-0.03 x US$50.9M, 2025). Reasoning: e-katalog TKDN preference and certified local makers on one side. On the other, ISO 13485 and izin edar barriers, and the Feb 2026 US deal exempting US goods from TKDN (the US supplies about a quarter of imports).
buyers: Kemenkes and regional (RSUD) hospitals via e-katalog
markets.jobs_note: No headcount found. Marthys' plant could make 664 device types (Dec 2022). Implant machining needs skilled CNC and EDM operators, QA and cleanroom packing staff.

markets.product: Prosthetics and orthotics (sockets, limbs, braces, custom insoles)
markets.local_now: Unknown. Small local makers hold TKDN certificates for prosthetic legs and hands (CV Isipa 36-38%, PT Ibrahim Rehabilitasi Servis 38%) and orthoses (Jayamas cervical collar 45.05%, Pratama Sentra Rehabilitasi TLSO). No local 3D-printed socket or orthosis maker was found. HS 902139 covers all artificial body parts other than joints. Orthoses sit in 902110 with implants, so this segment's trade figures are a loose proxy.
markets.cnc_3d_role: 3D scanning plus FDM/SLS printing of sockets, covers, wrist-hand orthoses and insoles. CNC makes pylons, adapters and foam or plaster positive moulds.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): 10-25% of new fittings at Java hospital and O&P workshops use scan-and-print within 5 years. Import substitution is small (902139 imports US$1.8M in 2025). Reasoning: the products are per-patient and local by nature. Printing cuts plaster casting and visits, but clinician (O&P) capacity, not machines, is the bottleneck.
markets.jobs_note: Labour-intensive clinical work. Printing shifts hours from plaster moulding to scanning and CAD.

markets.product: Hearing-aid shells and custom earmoulds
markets.local_now: About 0% for the devices: no hearing aid appears in the TKDN database (searched 16 Oct 2026). Comtrade estimates 20,566 units imported in 2025. Local custom-shell or earmould printing is unknown.
markets.cnc_3d_role: Ear-impression scans go to SLA/DLP-printed custom in-the-ear shells and earmoulds. The electronics are imported.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): custom shells and earmoulds 20-40% printed locally in clinic labs within 3-5 years, but under 5% of 902140 value. The electronics stay imported, and devices dominate the value.
markets.jobs_note: Very small (a few technicians per lab).

markets.product: Jewellery: castable wax/resin patterns and CAD masters for gold and silver
markets.local_now: Already in use in Bali. Celuk's government silver centre (Kemenperin and Pemkab Gianyar, built 2016/2018, revitalised 2022) has 3D design, 3D printing, CNC engraving and milling, laser and casting. Celuk has 152 IKM units, 2,364 workers, 4,515 kg a year and Rp158bn turnover (Warta Ekonomi, 23 Apr 2025). Flow Jewelry Studio (Denpasar, over 50 staff) does hand wax carving and 3D printing for global private-label clients, with Solidscape as its partner. The share of patterns printed nationally is unknown. HS 7113 exports were US$7.84bn in 2025 against US$54M of imports.
local_makers: Sentra IKM Perak Celuk shared facility (Gianyar)
Flow Jewelry Studio / PT DMD Asia (Denpasar)
PT Untung Bersama Sejahtera / UBS (city not stated on its site)
markets.cnc_3d_role: Castable-resin or wax printing (SLA/DLP, material jetting) and CNC wax milling make the lost-wax casting patterns. CNC also does diamond-cut faceting and master-mould work.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): within 3-5 years, 40-70% of new-design pattern-making digital (printed or CNC-milled wax) at large gold factories and export studios, and 15-30% in craft clusters such as Celuk and Kotagede. Celuk already has a shared 3D-printing and CNC facility. This is process share, not import substitution. It protects an export base that grew from US$5.29bn (2024) to US$7.84bn (2025).
markets.jobs_note: Digital patterns cut hand-carving hours. Setting, polishing and finishing stay labour-intensive. Celuk alone has 2,364 workers in 152 IKM units (2025).

markets.product: Rapid tooling: printed bridge-tool inserts and metal-AM conformal-cooling inserts for plastic moulds
markets.local_now: Mould localisation was about 45% in 2013 (IMDIA, snippet, older than 2023). No AM-tooling user was found. Kemenperin's SIINas counts about 660 mould and die firms with 35,000-40,000 units a year of capacity (Oct 2025).
markets.cnc_3d_role: CNC and EDM make mould bases and cavities. 3D printing adds printed polymer inserts for 50-500-shot bridge tools, metal-AM conformal-cooling inserts finished by CNC and EDM, and printed masters for silicone and vacuum casting.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): AM-assisted tooling addresses 2-5% of 848071+848079 import value, about US$6.4-15.9M at the 2025 level of US$318.6M (0.02-0.05 x 318.6), within 3-5 years. The larger prize is CNC mould making itself (see the CNC research).
markets.jobs_note: Skilled toolroom jobs (CNC, EDM, mould design). About 42,000 workers in mould and die firms (SIINas, Oct 2025).

markets.product: Foundry patterns, core boxes and printed sand moulds
markets.local_now: Unknown. Ceper (Klaten) foundries face a shortage of pattern and mould makers ('napel') (snippet). The Batur Jaya cooperative (Klaten) counts 168 foundry SMEs with 4,500 workers (snippet, date not given).
local_makers: Ceper foundry cluster, Koperasi Batur Jaya (Klaten)
markets.cnc_3d_role: Patterns and core boxes are CNC-milled from wood, resin board or aluminium, or 3D-printed (FDM/SLA) for short runs and complex cores. Binder-jet sand printing can skip patterns for prototypes.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): 10-25% of imported moulding patterns replaced by local CNC+printed patterns within 3-5 years, about US$1.1-2.7M at the 2025 level of US$10.8M. Reasoning: pattern-maker shortage in Ceper, patterns are bulky to ship, and imports fell from US$22.2M (2024) to US$10.8M (2025).
markets.jobs_note: Pattern making is skilled work. Digital patterns could relieve the napel shortage rather than cut jobs.

markets.product: Drone airframes, parts and payload mounts
markets.local_now: Unknown share. At least six TKDN-certified local drone makers exist, at 25-57% TKDN (searched 16 Oct 2026). 3DPrint.id lists drone and survey firms Aeroterrascan and Aerogeosurvey as clients.
markets.cnc_3d_role: 3D printing for prototypes, brackets, gimbal and payload mounts, ducts and low-volume housings. CNC for carbon plates, motor mounts and the moulds for composite airframes.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): local drones 10-20% of 8806 import value, about US$10-19M at the 2025 level of US$96.6M, within 3-5 years, concentrated in agricultural and survey drones. Military UAVs (Türkiye and Cyprus supplied 30% in 2025) stay imported. Printed and machined parts are about 10-20% of a local drone's bill of materials (judgement).
certs_needed: DGCA/Kemenhub drone registration and operating rules (not verified)
markets.jobs_note: Assembly, composite layup, machining and test pilots. No headcount found.

markets.product: Teaching aids and anatomical / medical training models
markets.local_now: Unknown. Local TKDN makers exist for anatomical and school teaching aids: CV Berkat Anugrah at 41-66%, CV Inti Citra Usaha at 38-40%. No 3D-printed product is among them. 902300 covers all demonstration apparatus and models, not only printed models.
markets.cnc_3d_role: Printed anatomical and dental phantoms, organ and surgical-planning models, and science and maths teaching models. CNC and laser make MDF and acrylic kits.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): 10-25% of 902300 imports replaced within 3-5 years, about US$2.5-6.2M at the 2025 level of US$25.0M. Reasoning: imports already fell from US$53.7M (2023), TKDN makers exist, and UGM shows medical-faculty demand (anatomy and cardiology products, dental phantoms).
markets.jobs_note: Small-batch printing and finishing jobs, spread across many SMEs.

markets.product: Construction 3D printing (3DCP) of walls, small buildings and street furniture
markets.local_now: Pilot stage. The Indocement Collaborative Hub (about 120 m2) was printed by Modula3D with a COBOD BOD3 printer (Aug 2025). Autoconz lists a 3DCP bench at Banjaratma rest area and giant lettering at UNU Yogyakarta. The same detik article links a story on a 3D-printed bus stop in Bali finished in four days. A TKDN-certified 3DCP mortar (AUTOCONZ, 68.29%) exists.
local_makers: Autoconz / PT Berdikari Teknologi Indonesia (Sleman and Bantul, DIY)
markets.cnc_3d_role: Gantry printers extrude special mortar. CNC plays a minor role (formwork, moulds for openings).
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): under 1% of wall construction within 5 years. Niches are public facilities, bus stops, feature walls and fast low-rise builds. Modula3D claims a simple house in 6 days and over 70% less wall time (Aug 2025).
certs_needed: building permit (PBG) and structural approval (not verified)
markets.jobs_note: Cuts masonry labour per wall and adds printer-operator and materials jobs.

markets.product: Product prototyping, jigs and fixtures, and low-volume end-use parts for manufacturers
markets.local_now: A service market of unknown size. Service bureaus and resellers list manufacturer clients. 3DPrint.id (Bandung, since 2015) names Astra Honda Motor, Laksana Karoseri, Formulatrix and XL Axiata. Raja 3D (Jakarta) shows Omron, Bayer Indonesia, PGN and LAPAN. A TKDN-certified e-KTP reader uses resin-3D-printed casings (Softorb, 33.48%). Indonesia exported US$44M of jigs and fixtures in Jan-Aug 2022 (Kemenperin, snippet, older than 2023).
local_makers: FOMU 3D Print / PT FOMU Karya Bersama (Jakarta Barat)
Raja 3D / PT Kirana Sakti Komputindo (Jakarta Selatan)
PT Softorb Technology Indonesia (Jakarta Barat, user)
markets.cnc_3d_role: FDM and resin printing for prototypes, assembly jigs, gauges, end-of-arm tooling and enclosures. CNC for metal fixtures and production versions.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): local bureaus can hold 70-90% of domestic prototyping and jig work within 3-5 years because turnaround beats imports. Growth is limited by thin SLS/MJF and metal capacity, which was not found locally.
markets.jobs_note: Design-heavy jobs (CAD, printing, finishing). No headcount data.

markets.product: Architectural and property scale models (maket)
markets.local_now: Service market of unknown size. FOMU 3D Print (Jakarta Barat, 70+ machines, since 2015) lists 'maket arsitektur' work, with logos including Intiland, AECOM and Kementerian PUPR. 3DPrint.id (Bandung) lists SHAU Architects and Jaya Real Property as clients. The TKDN database lists educational 'maket' products made of MDF and acrylic, not printed ones.
local_makers: FOMU 3D Print / PT FOMU Karya Bersama (Jakarta Barat)
markets.cnc_3d_role: FDM and resin printing for buildings, terrain and details. Laser and CNC cutting for bases, acrylic and MDF.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): 30-60% of model-making hours in Jakarta and Bandung studios move to printing within 3-5 years. No import base: this is a local service, so the gain is productivity and quality, not import substitution.
markets.jobs_note: Model makers shift from hand-cutting to CAD and print finishing.

markets.product: Spare parts on demand (obsolete polymer and metal parts for plants, mills, mines and rail)
markets.local_now: Unknown. No Indonesian on-demand spare-parts programme using 3D printing was found in this research.
markets.cnc_3d_role: Reverse engineering (3D scanning), printing of polymer parts and casting patterns, and CNC machining of metal replacements.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced, low confidence): 1-3% of MRO spares within 3-5 years, mostly obsolete polymer parts and casting patterns. Reasoning: there is no evidence base yet, and qualifying parts for plant use takes time.
markets.jobs_note: No data.

markets.product: Custom-fit eyewear frames
markets.local_now: Unknown. No local 3D-printed eyewear maker was found.
markets.cnc_3d_role: SLS/MJF nylon or resin printing of frames, then dyeing and hinge assembly. CNC for metal parts.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): 0-3% of frame imports, about US$0-1.2M at the 2025 level of US$40.6M. Niche custom and fashion frames only. No SLS/MJF capacity was found locally.
markets.jobs_note: Very small.

markets.product: Toys, figures and collectibles (custom and small-batch), plus prototypes for toy exporters
markets.local_now: Indonesia is a net toy exporter (US$651M exports vs US$344M imports in 2025). 3D-printed toy making is at hobby and SME level, for example the Bambu Lab creative hub at Urban Republic Dago, Bandung (Aug 2026).
markets.cnc_3d_role: FDM and resin printing for sculpts, prototypes and short runs. CNC makes the steel injection moulds for mass production.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): under 0.5% of toy market value. The real role is sculpt and prototype work for exporters and SME custom goods.
markets.jobs_note: Creator and SME jobs. Each is small.

markets.product: 3D-printing filament and resin materials
markets.local_now: Unknown. 391690 is a broad proxy: monofilament over 1 mm, rods and profiles of other plastics, not only 3D filament. 3D Zaiku runs a filament store (3dfilament.co.id). ITS and UGM student teams made filament from plastic waste (UGM, Jul 2024).
markets.cnc_3d_role: Extrusion of PLA, PETG and PP filament and formulation of resins. Not a CNC product.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): 10-20% of local filament demand from local extruders within 3-5 years, mostly PETG/PP and recycled grades. PLA resin is not made locally (inference).
markets.jobs_note: Small extrusion lines (a few workers each).

markets.product: Aerospace and defence MRO parts (tooling, interior and non-structural parts)
markets.local_now: Unknown. PT DI signed a framework with the Yogyakarta machine builder YPTI (12 Mar 2025, snippet). No aerospace AM user was found in sources.
markets.cnc_3d_role: Printed drill and assembly jigs, cabin and interior parts, and ducting. Certified metal AM flight parts need OEM and DGCA approval, so CNC remains the main route for metal parts.
markets.potential_share: Judgement (not sourced): 0.5-2% of 880730 import value, about US$2-9M at the 2025 level of US$438M, within 3-5 years. Mostly tooling and non-structural parts. Certification gates everything else.
markets.jobs_note: Few, high-skill jobs.

markets.product: Medical, surgical, dental and veterinary instruments (HS 9018)
markets.local_now: No HS-9018-specific share. Kemenkes: domestic devices were 48% of device use in 2024 vs 12% in 2019 (Farmalkes, 4 Jul 2025); about 20% of ~56,000 registered devices are made locally (Bisnis, Jun 2025, snippet); 812 domestic device producers (Apr 2025). Locally certified surgical instrument sets score low TKDN (Karya Medis FIMED/HAGEN sets 24-27%, i.e. mostly imported instruments), while Marthys's CNC-made orthopaedic instrument sets score 80-86%.
local_makers: PT Jayamas Medica Industri Tbk / OneMed (Krian, Sidoarjo)
PT Marthys Orthopaedic Indonesia (Prigen, Pasuruan) - orthopaedic instrument sets
PT Jenco Mulia Teknologi (Kota Depok) - surgical instrument sets 16-40%
PT Moftech Medical System (Jatinom, Klaten) - stainless surgical, dental and midwifery instrument sets 34-40%
PT Esa Behrindo Atmi Jaya (city not checked) - instrument set 40%
PT Asvia Laguna Medis (city not checked)
markets.cnc_3d_role: CNC: reusable stainless and titanium hand instruments (forceps, retractors, bone and orthopaedic instruments, dental hand instruments) by 5-axis milling, sliding-head turning and wire EDM, then grinding and passivation; instrument trays. 3D: patient-specific surgical guides and anatomical models printed in resin or nylon, plus jigs and prototypes. Most 9018 value (electromedical equipment, syringes, needles, catheters) is not CNC work.
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: local makers could supply about 5-10% of HS 9018 import value, US$36.9-73.9M (= 5-10% x US$738.7M), mostly reusable instrument sets and dental hand instruments sold through the TKDN-weighted e-catalogue. Reasoning: domestic devices already reached 48% of use in 2024, but local instrument sets are still largely imported (24-27% TKDN), so CNC instrument making is the open gap; Marthys shows CNC instrument sets can reach 80-86% TKDN. Limits: electromedical and disposable items dominate 9018 value and are not CNC work; the US deal (signed Feb 2026, not in force) would exempt US-origin devices (15% of 2025 imports) from TKDN preference.
buyers: Kemenkes and public hospitals via the sectoral e-catalogue (TKDN counted; imports were frozen in 2022)
Regional (RSUD) and private hospitals paid through BPJS/JKN (payment rules not sourced)
Export: Singapore 24%, USA 23%, Malaysia 11% of 2025 HS 9018 exports (Comtrade, via earlier notes)
certs_needed: Instrument-grade stainless steel per ISO 7153-1 (industry norm, not sourced here)
markets.jobs_note: Adds skilled jobs: CNC machinists, grinders and polishers, cleaning and passivation, QA and regulatory staff. Instrument finishing stays labour-intensive even with CNC. No headcount was sourced.

markets.product: Orthopaedic and fracture devices and artificial joints (HS 902110, 902131)
markets.local_now: No measured market share. Marthys (Dec 2022, older than 2023) targeted ~15% share with one machine and said more machines could take it above 50%. As of Oct 2026 four makers hold TKDN certificates covering plates, screws, nails, spinal systems, external fixators and hemi-hip prostheses. Marthys alone lists about 140 product lines at 35.6-98.3% (sibling notes' registry count).
markets.cnc_3d_role: CNC is the core process: sliding-head (Swiss-type) lathes for cortical, locking, cannulated and pedicle screws; 5-axis milling for locking and CMF plates; wire EDM. Risa lists CNC milling, CNC lathes, wire EDM and multi-axis machining of Ti-6Al-4V. 3D: metal powder-bed printing for patient-specific or porous implants (no local maker found) and resin or nylon printing of anatomical models and cutting guides for surgical planning.
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: 30-50% of trauma devices (902110), US$10.2-17.0M (= 30-50% x US$34.0M) of 2025 import value displaced, and 5-15% of artificial joints (902131), US$0.8-2.5M (= 5-15% x US$16.9M). Reasoning: four TKDN-certified makers already cover the full trauma range (plates, screws, nails, ex-fix) at 38-98% TKDN, and the e-catalogue favours them; combined imports grew from US$34.6M (2023) to US$50.9M (2025), so demand is rising. Joints are harder: only hemi-hip/bipolar prostheses are certified locally, and surgeons prefer established brands. Limits: titanium bar is imported (Marthys, 2022); the US deal would exempt US-origin implants (25% of 2025 imports) from TKDN preference if ratified.
buyers: Public hospitals via the Kemenkes sectoral e-catalogue (TKDN counted; imported listings can be frozen)
Hospitals doing JKN-funded trauma and spine surgery (payment rules not sourced)
certs_needed: Implant-grade material certificates, e.g. ASTM F136 Ti-6Al-4V ELI and ASTM F138 316LVM (industry norm, not sourced here)
ISO 10993 biocompatibility (industry norm, not sourced here)
markets.jobs_note: Adds high-skill jobs: CNC programmers and operators, metrology, cleaning and passivation, sterile packing, regulatory staff. Marthys tied market share to machine count (one machine, ~15% target, Dec 2022), so jobs scale with machines added. No headcount was sourced.

markets.product: Other prostheses and orthoses (HS 902139, other artificial body parts; orthopaedic braces fall partly in 902110)
markets.local_now: Trade data barely captures this line (2025 imports small), because limb prostheses and orthoses are mostly fitted by local workshops as a service. TKDN-certified makers found: CV Isipa (Kota Jambi) for prosthetic legs (36%) and hands (38%); PT Pratama Sentra Rehabilitasi (Tangerang Selatan) for spinal orthoses and collars (40%); and OneMed for a truncal orthosis and cervical collar (45.05%). Searches for 'prostesis' found nothing. Indonesia also exported US$10-11M a year under 902139 in 2024-2025; the products and the exporter were not identified. The 2025 exports went to USA 39%, Singapore 20%, Germany 20%, Belgium 11%; the exporter was not identified.
local_makers: CV Isipa (Kota Jambi) - prosthetic legs and hands
PT Pratama Sentra Rehabilitasi (Kota Tangerang Selatan) - lumbar corsets, TLSO, neck collars
PT Jayamas Medica Industri Tbk / OneMed (Krian, Sidoarjo) - truncal orthosis and cervical collar
PT Ibrahim Rehabilitasi Servis (Tuban) - prosthetic hands 38%
markets.cnc_3d_role: 3D: scan-to-print prosthetic sockets, orthotic insoles, ankle-foot orthoses, scoliosis braces and cranial helmets; patient-specific cranial plates in PEEK or titanium (hospital-led). CNC: knee and ankle joints, pylons and adapters in aluminium or titanium; CNC carving of foam positive moulds.
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: 3D-printed sockets, insoles and orthoses could reach 20-40% of new fittings in hospital orthotic-prosthetic units, but the value cannot be sized, because fittings are a service not seen in trade data (2025 imports were only US$1.8M). Reasoning: printing needs only a scanner, CAD and a printer per clinic, and the trade-visible import base is tiny, so this is a service-and-jobs opportunity rather than import substitution. No source gives the number of fittings per year.
buyers: Hospital orthotic-prosthetic units and workshops (not sourced)
certs_needed: Kemenkes marketing authorisation (izin edar, AKD) for prosthetic components
ISO 10328 structural testing of lower-limb prostheses (industry norm, not sourced here)
markets.jobs_note: Adds jobs: orthotist-prosthetist technicians, 3D scanning and CAD staff, print-finishing technicians. Printing shortens fitting time, but each fitting still needs a clinician. No headcount was sourced.

markets.product: Hearing aids (HS 902140)
markets.local_now: About 0%: Kemenperin's TKDN registry has no certified hearing aid (searches 'alat bantu dengar' and 'hearing aid', 16 Oct 2026). 2025 imports were about 20,566 units at roughly US$138 each CIF (estimate: Comtrade quantity field read as units; 2.83M / 20,566).
markets.cnc_3d_role: 3D: custom in-the-ear shells and earmolds printed in biocompatible resin from ear scans (the standard global method; no Indonesian lab was found). Electronics (sound processor, receiver, battery) stay imported. CNC role is minor (moulds for behind-the-ear housings).
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: 5-15% of units (about 1,000-3,100 of ~20,600 units a year, estimate) could be locally finished, with custom shells or earmolds printed in Indonesian clinics; the local value share would be lower because the electronics stay imported. Reasoning: at ~US$2.8M of imports a year the market is too small for a factory, but a shell and earmold print service needs little capital. No local maker exists today.
buyers: Audiology clinics and hearing-aid retailers (not sourced)
certs_needed: IEC 60118 hearing-aid performance (industry norm, not sourced here)
markets.jobs_note: Small: shell-printing and fitting jobs inside clinics. No factory-scale jobs at ~20,000 units a year.

markets.product: Dental devices and lab work: artificial teeth and dental fittings (HS 902121, 902129), plus clear aligners and crowns (not separately visible in trade data)
markets.local_now: No share figure. The trade-visible base is tiny (dental fittings; 902129 is mostly dental implants from Korea). No TKDN-certified dental implant, denture or aligner exists (registry, Oct 2026). Locally certified: dental chairs and units (Andini Sarana 44-50%, ATMI Solo 43-44%, Karya Medis 40-41%) and hand instruments (OneMed 54.2%). Clear aligners: Rata (Jakarta) claims 70,000+ patients and 100+ clinics in 50+ cities, but does not say where aligners are made. Crowns and dentures come from dental labs; no data was found.
local_makers: Rata (Kebayoran Baru, Jakarta Selatan) - clear aligners
PT Andini Sarana (Jakarta Timur) - dental units
PT ATMI Solo (Kota Surakarta) - dental chairs
PT Karya Medis Nusantara (Kota Tangerang) - dental units
PT Jayamas Medica Industri Tbk / OneMed (Krian, Sidoarjo) - dental hand instruments
UGM engineering and dentistry faculties (Sleman) - dental phantoms and dental 3D printing (R&D)
markets.cnc_3d_role: Both. CNC: 5-axis dental mills cut zirconia, PMMA and titanium crowns, bridges and implant abutments (CAD/CAM); sliding-head lathes machine titanium implant fixtures. 3D: resin printers make aligner models (each aligner is thermoformed over a printed model), surgical guides, dentures and temporary crowns. Dental instruments (HS 901849) are counted in the 9018 line.
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years, by segment: (a) clear aligners: 50-80% of Indonesian cases could be produced in-country (printed models plus thermoforming), because providers like Rata already run local clinics and scans; (b) crowns: CAD/CAM milling and printing could reach 30-50% of crowns made by Indonesian labs (current share unknown); (c) dental implants (902129, 2025 imports US$1.4M, Korea-led): from 0% to 5-10% only if a local maker registers an implant. The import base is too small to matter; the opportunity is lab services and jobs, not import substitution.
buyers: Private dental clinics and chains (e.g. Rata's 100+ clinics and partners)
Patients paying out of pocket (Rata aligners from Rp5.9 million vs Rp20 million for braces)
Hospital dental units; public purchases of chairs and instruments via the e-catalogue
certs_needed: ISO 6872 dental ceramics and ISO 22674 dental alloys (industry norm, not sourced here)
markets.jobs_note: Adds jobs: CAD designers, dental technicians, mill and printer operators. Aligner and crown work is local by nature because it is patient-specific. No headcount was sourced.

markets.product: Precious-metal jewellery (HS 7113), made with 3D-printed wax or resin patterns
markets.local_now: Domestic supply dominates: 2025 imports were US$54.4M against exports of US$7,839.8M, so imports equal 0.7% of exports; no measured domestic market share. Exports rose 42% from 2023 to 2025 (gold-type 711319 US$7,647.4M; silver 711311 US$192.1M, up from US$104.6M). The 2025 export unit value of 711319 was about US$93,249 per kg (estimate: US$7,647.4M / 82,010 kg reported), consistent with high-carat gold pieces. Gold-type exports (711319) went to Switzerland 51%, Singapore 15%, United Arab Emirates 13%, China, Hong Kong SAR 8%; silver (711311) to Japan 47%, Thailand 22%, USA 15%, Germany 4% (2025).
local_makers: Sentra IKM Kerajinan Perak Celuk (Celuk, Gianyar) - Kemenperin/Pemkab centre with CNC engraving and milling, 3D printing and laser machines; 152 IKM units, 2,364 workers
Flow Jewelry Studio / PT DMD Asia (Denpasar) - CAD and 3D-printed wax, lost-wax casting, private label
SUNSRI House of Jewelry (Celuk, Gianyar) - 3D design and printing, lost-wax casting
BBKB Yogyakarta, Kemenperin (Kota Yogyakarta) - public 3D-printed resin masters and silver casting service
PT Untung Bersama Sejahtera / UBS (city not stated on its site)
markets.cnc_3d_role: 3D: CAD-designed pieces printed as castable resin or wax patterns, then lost-wax cast. This cuts model-making time and allows short runs, personalisation and fast design cycles (UBS releases new designs every two weeks). CNC: diamond-cut faceting, engraving, ring and bangle turning; laser welding and marking. Machine-made chain and high-carat commodity pieces, likely much of the export value, use chain machines and casting rather than 3D (inference).
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: the import share is already tiny, so the target is process share. About 25-50% of design-led cast pieces from Java and Bali workshops could move to CAD plus 3D-printed resin or wax patterns. Replacing 5-15% of branded 711319 imports (US$39.4M, mostly Italy, USA, Switzerland, France) would add only US$2.0-5.9M (= 5-15% x US$39.4M). Reasoning: castable-resin printing needs little capital and fits fast design cycles (UBS launches designs every two weeks). Public capacity already exists: Celuk's Kemenperin/Gianyar centre has CNC, 3D-printing and laser machines (2025), and BBKB Yogyakarta prints resin masters and casts silver as a service (2026). Kotagede needs ways to attract young artisans. High-carat commodity and machine-chain exports, likely most of the US$7.6bn, gain less from 3D. The export mix (half to Switzerland, a refining and trading hub, plus Singapore, the UAE and Hong Kong) suggests much of the gold value is high-carat, commodity-like jewellery (inference).
buyers: Export destinations 2025 (Comtrade): Switzerland 50%, Singapore 14%, United Arab Emirates 13%, China, Hong Kong SAR 8%, Jordan 5%
Domestic gold-jewellery retail and e-commerce (UBS sells via its own site, Tokopedia and Shopee)
Tourist and gallery retail in Kotagede (Yogyakarta) and Celuk (Bali)
certs_needed: Gold fineness and assay marking for buyers (no Indonesian SNI checked)
Responsible-gold due diligence such as OECD guidance or RJC certification (industry norm, not sourced here)
markets.jobs_note: Adds design jobs (CAD jewellery designers, printer operators) and keeps casting and finishing jobs; it may replace some hand wax carving. Kotagede struggles to attract young artisans (snippet), so CAD and 3D may make the trade more attractive. No headcount was sourced.

markets.product: Imitation jewellery (HS 7117)
markets.local_now: Unknown. 2025 imports of US$30.4M exceed exports of US$17.1M, and imports grew 38% from 2023; 'other' imitation jewellery (711790) comes 81% from China. No maker is named (TKDN registry hits are sole proprietors).
markets.cnc_3d_role: 3D-printed masters for brass, zamak or pewter casting; fibre-laser cutting and CNC engraving of stainless and brass sheet pieces; small-batch fashion lines and personalised pieces.
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: 15-30% of imports, US$4.6-9.1M (= 15-30% x US$30.4M), could be replaced by locally designed cast or laser-cut fashion jewellery. Reasoning: low entry barriers (desktop resin printers, small fibre lasers) and local fashion and souvenir demand. Limit: Chinese price competition on basic pieces.
buyers: Export destinations 2025 (Comtrade): Philippines 20%, France 12%, USA 9%, Spain 8%, Singapore 7%
Domestic fashion and souvenir retail and e-commerce (not sourced)
certs_needed: EU REACH limits on nickel, lead and cadmium (industry norm, not sourced here)
US CPSIA for children's jewellery (industry norm, not sourced here)
markets.jobs_note: Adds design and finishing jobs; laser cutting replaces some hand sawing and filing. No headcount was sourced.

markets.product: Furniture (HS 9403), CNC-routed
markets.local_now: Net exporter: 2025 exports US$1,119.8M against imports of US$532.4M. Imports rose 39% from 2023 (US$384.2M), led by 'other metal furniture' (940320, US$145.3M to US$277.2M); wooden-furniture imports stayed small. Exports slipped from US$1,160.1M (2023). No measured domestic market share. Import origins 2025: China 92%, Malaysia 2%, Italy 1%, Viet Nam 1%.
local_makers: Jepara carving and furniture firms (Jepara): 387 large and 3,438 small/medium carving businesses (2020)
CV Solobeat Internasional (Depok, Sleman) - school and office furniture with TKDN
PT ATMI Solo (Kota Surakarta) - metal workshop furniture with TKDN
Kab. Cirebon rattan and wood furniture firms (Cirebon): 1,520 rattan and 1,441 wood-furniture firms, 65,696 rattan workers (2023)
PT Woodpark Mebel Perkasa (KEK Industropolis Batang) - Rp225 bn plant due Apr 2027; clients B&B Italia, Arhaus, RH
PT Panca Karya Unggul Abadi and two related firms (Cileungsi, Bogor) - TKDN items for CNC-cut HPL backdrops
markets.cnc_3d_role: CNC routers and nesting lines cut MDF and plywood panels for flat-pack, office, school and hotel furniture; 5-axis routers shape chair parts and carved panels; CNC tenoners and boring lines do joinery. Mostly labour-saving per unit: in one Jepara trial a 5 m carved wall took 3 months by hand and 8-9 days by CNC (2020 snippet).
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: 15-30% of furniture imports, US$79.9-159.7M (= 15-30% x US$532.4M), could be replaced by local CNC panel and metal-furniture makers. Reasoning: the import surge is mostly metal furniture, which is laser-, tube- and press-brake work that Java metal shops can do; government and school furniture is bought by TKDN (e.g. Solobeat 43-64%). On exports, CNC mainly defends share: exports were flat to down 2023-2025, the US (57% of 2025 exports) has charged 19% on Indonesian goods since the July 2025 framework, furniture is not on the 0% list of the Feb 2026 deal, and IEU-CEPA is not yet in force.
buyers: Export markets 2025: USA 57%, Japan 9%, Netherlands 4%, Belgium 3% (Comtrade, via earlier notes)
Government, school and office buyers via the e-catalogue (TKDN)
Hotel, office and residential fit-out contractors (import substitution; not sourced)
certs_needed: EU deforestation regulation (EUDR) due diligence for the EU
Buyer product-safety and finish standards (not sourced)
markets.jobs_note: Labour-saving per unit. Only 8 of 390 medium Jepara firms used CNC in 2020, and a 2026 industry speaker expected the machine share to rise from ~50% toward ~80% (snippets). Reasoning: PLN already certifies in-house reverse-engineered parts, so drawings and acceptance routes exist; boiler-part imports (840290) fell from US$526.7M in 2023 to US$85.4M in 2025 as plant construction slowed, so the lasting pool is replacement parts; gas-turbine hot-section parts (841199, USA 42%) need OEM alloys and coatings and would be TKDN-exempt US goods under the ART.

markets.product: Jigs, fixtures, test nests and precision parts for electronics assembly lines
markets.local_now: Values are HS 846620 (work holders, a proxy; EMS fixtures are not separately coded). Local share: unknown. Smartphones sold in Indonesia need 35-40% TKDN, which drove assembly plants in Batam, Cikarang and Tangerang (Feb 2026).
markets.cnc_3d_role: CNC: aluminium and steel fixture plates, pallets and carriers, pogo-pin test-fixture frames, SMT stencil frames and conveyor parts. 3D: ESD-safe polymer nests, locating pins and covers, pick-and-place grippers and quick fixture iterations for new models (inference).
markets.potential_share: Judgement: 20-40% of imported work holders within 3-5 years, about US$3.6-7.2M a year (estimate: 17.9 x 0.20 = 3.6; 17.9 x 0.40 = 7.2), plus a share of test-fixture parts (903190, US$58.8M in 2025) and machine parts (847990, US$288.7M), both multi-industry. Reasoning: fixtures are made to order with short lead times, which favours shops near the plants; but EMS volumes depend on phone TKDN rules that the ART would lift for US brands.
buyers: EMS and electronics plants in Batam (e.g. PT Sat Nusapersada)
Assembly plants in Cikarang (Bekasi) and Tangerang (not named in sources)

markets.product: Car parts (HS 8708), especially machined parts: brakes, gearboxes, axles, wheels, suspension, steering
markets.local_now: GIAMM (31 Jul 2025): the local supply chain supplies about 55% of a car's value (Thailand about 78%), from about 1,550 suppliers plus 950 SMEs. No separate local share exists for machined parts. Certified electric cars sit at 40-46.5% TKDN (6 firms, Kemenperin TKDN database, 16 Oct 2026). 2025 imports (3,132.2) exceeded exports (2,133.3) (Comtrade, US$M).

Koperasi Batur Jaya foundries (Ceper, Kab. Klaten)

markets.cnc_3d_role: CNC turning and milling of brake discs, drums and calipers, hubs and knuckles, axle shafts, suspension and steering parts, gears and shafts, plus brackets for EV battery and motor mounting. The work is volume tier-2/3 machining under IATF 16949. 3D printing is a support role: jigs, welding fixtures, checking gauges and prototype brackets for the EV models that must reach 60% TKDN in 2027.
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: Indonesian-made share of machined car parts could rise about 5-10 percentage points from GIAMM's ~55% overall local content. That would replace 5-10% of 2025 HS 8708 imports, about US$157-313M (estimate: 0.05 x 3,132.2 and 0.10 x 3,132.2). The most machining-heavy codes (brakes 870830, axles 870850, wheels 870870, suspension 870880, steering 870894) imported US$1,173M in 2025. Gearboxes (870840) stay captive imports of Japanese and Thai groups. Reasoning: the 2027 EV step to 60% TKDN (all certified EV cars are at 40-46.5%), the 1:1 CBU-offset deadline at end-2027 and the car market recovery (+21% Jan-Sep 2026) pull work onshore. Against that, Japanese/Thai captive supply chains, IATF and PPAP approval lead times (often 12-24 months, industry norm, not sourced) and the scale cost gap with China and Thailand hold it back. Much of the gain will go to foreign tier-1s opening in West Java, with Indonesian CNC shops as tier-2/3.

markets.local_now: TKDN database (16 Oct 2026): 102 certified e-motorcycle models from 27 firms, all on Java. Median TKDN 46.4% (range 30.4-75.0%); only 15 models reach the 60% that applies from 1 Jan 2027. No sourced local share for motors, controllers or battery packs. Conversion: 194 conversions by Nov 2023 against a 1,000 target, with 13 licensed workshops (GGGI 2024). About 236,000 e-motorcycles on the road in Oct 2025, under 1% of the fleet (ESDM via Wikipedia).

markets.cnc_3d_role: CNC: hub-motor and mid-drive motor housings and end caps (die-cast then machined), shafts, swingarms and pivots, wheel hubs, brake mounts, battery-tray rails and terminals, controller heat-sink housings, conversion-kit motor mounts and adapter plates. 3D printing: fit-check prototypes of enclosures and brackets, low-volume (<1,000/yr) plastic covers and connector housings, sand-printed moulds for first-run aluminium housings, assembly fixtures.
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: if the 60% TKDN rule holds from 2027, locally made shares of machined/cast e-motorcycle metal parts (housings, swingarms, enclosures) in Indonesian-assembled models could reach 60-80%, from an unknown and probably lower base. Most certified models (median 46.4%) need about 14 more TKDN points, and cells and magnets are hard to localise, so metal parts are the cheapest points. The market is small. Estimate: 100,000 units/yr (the government's planned 2026 incentive quota) x Rp1.5-3.0M of machined/cast metal per unit (assumption) = Rp150-300 billion/yr, about US$9-18M at an assumed Rp16,500/US$. Complete e-2W imports (HS 871160) were US$21.2M in 2025, for scale. Conversion kits: 0-5% of this, since the programme stalled (194 conversions by Nov 2023). Reasoning: TKDN pull and planned incentives (Rp5M/unit for 100,000 units, not issued as of Aug 2026) versus weak demand (<1% of 6.41M sales in 2025) and cheap Chinese kits.

markets.product: Bicycles and bicycle parts (HS 8712, 871491-871499)
markets.local_now: Unknown as a sourced share, but trade shows local assembly dominates: complete bicycles (8712) were exported for US$129.8M and imported for only US$7.8M in 2025 (Comtrade). PT Insera Sena (Polygon, Kab. Sidoarjo) states an annual capacity of one million bicycles. Indonesia is a net exporter of hubs and free-wheels (871493: exports US$37.2M vs imports US$21.7M in 2025) but imports frames (871491: US$74.6M, exports US$3.7M) and rims and spokes (871492: US$39.6M). The TKDN database holds no bicycle certificates.
markets.cnc_3d_role: CNC: hubs, freewheel bodies, cranks and spiders, stems, seat-post heads, dropouts and head tubes for welded aluminium frames, e-bike motor mounts. Welding jigs (CNC-cut). 3D printing: prototype lugs and dropouts, fixtures, and possibly premium printed titanium/aluminium parts (no local evidence).
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: replace 15-30% of frame and fork imports (871491), about US$11-22M (estimate: 0.15 and 0.30 x US$74.6M), anchored on Polygon's Sidoarjo plant and e-bike exports. CNC parts beyond that are small. All bicycle and part imports were US$279.1M in 2025. Reasoning: an existing assembler with exports to the US and EU and a hub export base work for it. Taiwan/China frame costs and no public-procurement pull (no TKDN demand) work against it.
buyers: E-bike exporters (Polygon's first e-bike export to the USA/EU, Dec 2024)
certs_needed: SNI for bicycles (mandatory status not verified)
markets.jobs_note: No employee count found for Polygon or other bicycle makers. Capacity is 1M bicycles/yr (Insera Sena site).

markets.product: Farm machinery and parts (HS 8432, 8433, 8436, 8437; trade figures are the four headings, which include their parts lines 843290, 843390, 843699, 843790)
markets.local_now: TKDN database (16 Oct 2026): 60 firms hold 262 farm-machine certificates, 54 of them on Java. Median certified TKDN: 2-wheel tractors 52.6%, threshers 45.6%, rice milling units 40.8%, 4-wheel tractors 35.9%, transplanters 33.9%, combine harvesters 33.0%. Quick's hand tractors with Kubota RD diesels made in Semarang certify at up to 83.1%; its petrol-engined model is at 40.2%. Quick held up to 70% of the hand-tractor market in 2017 (snippet, pre-2023). Hand-tractor imports (870110) were only US$0.6M in 2025, so hand tractors are almost wholly made locally (Comtrade). Kemenperin: 67 firms, 5,629 workers, US$90M exports in 2024.
local_makers: CV Karya Hidup Sentosa/Quick (Kab. Kulon Progo)
PT Tri Ratna Diesel Indonesia (Kab. Gresik)
markets.cnc_3d_role: CNC: gears, shafts, sprockets and gearbox housings for hand tractors and rotavators; rotary blades, threshing drums and concaves; combine header and track-drive parts; pulleys; machined castings. 3D printing: patterns and core boxes for gearbox and housing castings, scan-to-CAD of worn spares for old Japanese and Chinese machines, prototypes.
markets.potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: replace 15-25% of 2025 imports of HS 8432, 8433, 8436 and 8437, about US$63-105M (estimate: 0.15 and 0.25 x US$419.6M). The gain would come by raising combines and 4-wheel tractors from ~33-36% TKDN toward 45-50% with locally machined drivetrain and threshing parts, and by more local hand tractors and threshers. Reasoning: Kementan is a large repeat buyer (7,676 combines in 2020-2026; 16,717 2-wheel and 8,396 4-wheel tractors; 56,000 pumps in 2026), Java makers already hold certificates, and China supplies most imports (cheap but distant support). Against that: Kementan's TKDN floor is only 25%, so imported kits qualify; import costs from China are low; and there is no local engine supply for larger tractors.

National titles: China Pump Hometown, China Small Air Compressor Hometown, China Tool City
Stock listings of anchor firms (Dayuan Pump 2017, Taifu Pump 2021) and an HKEX-listed tools trading-market company (2020)
clusters_world.lessons: The clearest 'one county, one machined product' case with fresh primary numbers: thousands of small firms, a dominant domestic share, and a 2020s upgrade layer (shared procurement, supply-chain finance, digital platform) built on a 40-year base. What transfers: shared services across many small shops. Not verified this round: workers, margins, price wars, pollution.

clusters_world.cluster: Yongkang hardware cluster (Hardware Capital, 五金之都)
clusters_world.product: Hardware: power tools, security doors, stainless tableware, scales, vacuum cups, scooters and leisure vehicles
clusters_world.firms: About 10,000 hardware firms (2009; via Wikipedia, citing Zhejiang Daily, 27 May 2009)
clusters_world.workers: About 300,000 (2009; same source). Estimate: about 30 workers per firm (300,000 / 10,000)
clusters_world.output: No hardware-only output found. City GDP CNY 83.55 billion in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
clusters_world.share: About one-third of China's power tools, 52% of stainless-steel tableware, 45% of daily-use scales (English Wikipedia, uncited, no year)
clusters_world.started: Old metal-craft tradition; modern private cluster after the 1978 reforms (no exact year found)
levers: China Science and Technology Hardware City wholesale market (described as China's largest hardware market)
Annual China Hardware Expo (26-28 Sep; 14 editions by 2009)
National product titles: China Door Capital (2009), China Leisure Sports Vehicle Capital (2009), China Cup Capital (2011)
Private firms (over 95% of output)
clusters_world.lessons: Market-plus-trade-fair model and product hopping (doors since 1997, scooters, cups). Titles came in 2009-2011, long after the cluster was large. Firm and worker counts are 17 years old; the national shares are uncited. Boom-bust episodes (e.g., scooters around 2000) were not verified this round.

clusters_world.product: Spectacle lenses and frames (also a drill-bit cluster, no figures found)
clusters_world.firms: More than 400 glasses factories around 1987 (36Kr, 5 Aug 2026); no current count found
clusters_world.output: 6.5 million pairs a year around 1987; glasses market turnover above CNY 1 billion a year in the 1990s; Wanxin Optical alone 100M+ resin lenses and CNY 1.2 billion+ sales a year, undated (36Kr, 5 Aug 2026)
clusters_world.share: About 50% of world and 75% of China's spectacle-lens output (36Kr, 5 Aug 2026; no year given for the shares)
clusters_world.started: 1960s (workshops seeded by educated youth from Suzhou and Shanghai glasses factories)
levers: County government opened two dedicated glasses wholesale markets (Huayang and Yunyang) near the railway station in 1986
Later: foreign capital and technology, R&D departments, optical industrial parks
Eyewear Characteristic Town from 2021 (CNY 8.5 billion+ invested)
E-commerce and live-streaming sales; Mingyue Lenses listed 2021
clusters_world.lessons: Market first: the 1986 county-built markets pulled scattered shack factories into a cluster. Weak points 60 years on: no strong own brand, mainly mid-to-low end, high-index resin monomer bought from Korea's KOC, 1.74-index technology held by Western makers, and mostly SMEs without a technology leader.

clusters_world.product: Plastic moulding base that grew into stationery (binder clips, hole punchers, pencil sharpeners)
clusters_world.firms: Anchor firm Deli; no firm count found
clusters_world.output: Stationery revenue CNY 8.6 billion in 2012 (via Wikipedia, citing MOFCOM, Sep 2013)
clusters_world.share: 80% of the world's binder clips; 10% of world hole punchers and pencil sharpeners; about 10% of China's stationery exports (via Wikipedia; years not stated)
clusters_world.started: Late 1980s (stationery built on an existing moulding industry)
levers: Existing mould-making capability
Anchor firm (Deli)
Export orientation (about 70% of output exported)
clusters_world.lessons: A process capability (moulding) seeded a product cluster, the closest Chinese precedent to 'capability first, products later'; but the product found the capability, it was not planned. No mould-specific figures found; numbers are 8-14 years old and second-hand.

clusters_world.cluster: Huangyan mould and plastics cluster (China Mould Hometown, 中国模具之乡)
clusters_world.product: Plastic injection moulds (auto, appliance, medical, TV, e-bike parts) and plastic daily-use products
clusters_world.share: '70% of plastic molds nationwide' as of 2006 (English Wikipedia, uncited; looks high, treat as unverified); about 50% of TV makers source TV moulds there (same page)
levers: National titles: China Mould Hometown, China Plastic Daily-Use Products Capital
Downstream anchor customers in autos and appliances (FAW, Geely, Dongfeng, Shanghai VW, Haier, Hisense named)
clusters_world.lessons: Mould capability served many downstream industries at once (TVs, e-bikes, cars, appliances). No verified firm count, output or start date this round; the 70% share is uncited and 20 years old.

clusters_world.product: Auto parts (largest industry) and water-and-heating valves (second)
clusters_world.firms: All industry, end 2017: 12,748 industrial firms, 743 above designated size, 139 above CNY 100 million (via Wikipedia, citing Yuhuan statistical bulletin, 8 Apr 2018)
clusters_world.output: All industry 2017: CNY 156.4 billion; above-scale CNY 69.8 billion (same source). No valve-only figure found
levers: Two named pillar industries (auto parts, valves) in the city's industrial structure
clusters_world.lessons: Two-product structure (auto parts plus valves) rather than one product. Valve output, share, workers and history were not verified this round; city-wide numbers are 9 years old.

clusters_world.cluster: Yuyao mould and plastics cluster (China Mould City, China Plastics City)
clusters_world.product: Plastic moulding, electric appliances, machinery (per English Wikipedia, uncited)
clusters_world.lessons: No verified figures this round (no search available; Wikipedia pages lack them). The China Mould City and China Plastics City markets were not verified. Needs a Chinese-language search before publishing.

clusters_world.cluster: Chang'an mould, hardware and electronics cluster
clusters_world.product: Export manufacturing; moulds, hardware and electronics (cluster identity not verified this round)
clusters_world.lessons: No verified industry figures. Context only: 594,809 people at the 2000 census (then China's most populous town) and 807,400 permanent residents in 2021 (Wikipedia). The town-profile page on dg.gov.cn failed DNS from this VM.

clusters_world.cluster: Tengzhou small and medium machine-tool cluster
clusters_world.product: Small and medium machine tools (cluster identity from the brief; not verified this round)
clusters_world.lessons: No verified machine-tool figures. English Wikipedia lists 254 above-scale industrial firms in 2019 (all industry), does not list machinery among major industries, and says many factories closed in an early-2010s downturn (citing WSJ, 20 Jul 2015, not fetched). Needs Chinese sources before publishing.

clusters_world.firms: Named makers: Creality (founded 2014), Bambu Lab (founded Aug 2020); EqualOcean also names Anycubic, Elegoo and Anker as sector leaders without giving their locations
clusters_world.output: Creality shipped 4.4 million printers in 2020-2024 (Wikipedia). Bambu Lab expected to reach about CNY 1.5 billion of revenue in 2023 (EqualOcean, 5 Jan 2024; a forecast, not a reported figure)
levers: Engineer spin-offs from an anchor firm (Bambu Lab's founders came from DJI's consumer drone unit)
Crowdfunding and direct-to-consumer exports (Bambu Lab X1 Kickstarter HK$55 million, 2022)
City-scale electronics supply chain (not quantified in the sources read)
clusters_world.lessons: Grew from Shenzhen's electronics ecosystem and spin-offs, not from a county one-product designation. IP friction is part of the model: Wikipedia cites reports of GPL complaints against Creality (2018) and an Artec lawsuit over a scanner (titles only, not fetched). Shenzhen's share of world output and metal 3D-printing clusters (Xi'an, Wuhan) were not verified.

clusters_world.product: Small commodities: a wholesale market platform rather than one product
clusters_world.firms: 75,000+ stores (Wikipedia infobox); 1,000+ vendors selling 3,000+ products by end-1983; booths above 10,000 in 1991
clusters_world.output: About US$11 billion of goods sold a year, 2013 (via Wikipedia)
clusters_world.share: Called 'the world's largest small commodities market' by the World Bank in 2005 (via Wikipedia)
levers: County Party secretary legalised a free market in 1982
County spent CNY 580,000 in 1983 to build a booth market
Market trading declared the pillar industry in 1984
Government-owned market buildings (owner: Yiwu Municipal Government)
clusters_world.lessons: The archetype of the specialised-market lever: local government organised trade first, and most goods were made elsewhere at the start. For CNC and 3D printing, the analogue is an order-matching hub that aggregates buyers for many small shops.

clusters_world.product: Shoes, lighters, low-voltage electrical goods, other light industry
levers: Private family firms and informal finance
Local-government clean-ups of counterfeit goods (late 1980s; 1994 'second start-up')
clusters_world.lessons: Failure case. Counterfeit and substandard goods in the late 1980s forced a nationwide clean-up. From 2010, tighter credit broke firms' cash flows, guarantee companies and mutual-guarantee networks were hit in succession, and local government had to step in (Wikipedia). Cluster finance works in a boom and breaks in a credit squeeze.

clusters_world.cluster: Taichung precision machinery and machine-tool cluster
clusters_world.product: Machine tools, mechanical components, woodworking machinery, bicycles
clusters_world.output: Precision machinery called Taiwan's 'third trillion-dollar (NT$) industry' (Chinese Wikipedia, citing a 2009 note; no figure checked)
clusters_world.started: 1960s (Taichung Port, Taichung Industrial Park, an export processing zone and Freeway No. 1 supported small factories)
levers: Public infrastructure in the 1960s (port, industrial park, export processing zone, freeway)
Taichung Industrial Park (Xitun); city-built Precision Machinery Technology Innovation Park phases 1-2 (Nantun)
Central Taiwan Science Park from 2002
clusters_world.lessons: The nearest machine-tool analogue. It survived a late-1980s/1990s hollowing-out, when many makers moved to mainland China and Southeast Asia. Firm counts, workers, output and the 'golden valley' radius were not verified this round.

clusters_world.product: Many local products, one chosen per village or town (farm, food and craft products)
clusters_world.firms: OVOP products: 143 in 1980, 336 in 2001 (Haraguchi 2008, UNIDO, p. 9)
clusters_world.output: OVOP product sales US$330 million in 1980, US$1,300 million in 2001 (Haraguchi 2008, p. 9). Estimate: 3.9x in 21 years
clusters_world.started: 1979 (Governor Morihiko Hiramatsu; implementation from 1980; modelled on Oyama town's 1961 NPC movement)
levers: Community-led product choice
Coordinating organisations giving technical and marketing advice, sometimes running jointly owned equipment for capital-intensive processing
Prefecture gives only supplementary support: extension services, learning activities, product promotion
clusters_world.lessons: Income per head rose from 1.405 million yen (1980) to 2.798 million yen (2000), then 2.647 million yen (2003), and Oita rose from 3rd to 1st of Kyushu's 7 prefectures; Haraguchi says OVOP 'seems to have contributed' (a judgement, not a causal estimate). Slow and dependent on community leadership, but sustainable with local linkages. Not about machining.

clusters_world.product: One starred product per tambon (food, crafts, textiles, household goods)
clusters_world.firms: 36,000 OTOP groups of 30-3,000 members each (Wikipedia, uncited); 569 five-star products
clusters_world.output: Sales THB 33.3 billion (2003), THB 46.3 billion (2004), THB 38.5 billion (9 months of 2005) (Haraguchi 2008, Table 3); THB 153 billion (2017; Bangkok Post via Wikipedia)
levers: Central-government administration (National OTOP Administrative Committee in the Prime Minister's Office)
Star ratings and OTOP Product Champion quality grades
Trade fairs and export promotion
Budget THB 0.8 billion (2003), 1.5 billion (2004); THB 1.24 billion (FY2018) falling to THB 363 million (FY2020)
clusters_world.lessons: Faster results than Oita but less sustainable. Market saturation with similar products; officials favoured already-advantaged producers; some products were registered without producers' consent to pad the numbers (Haraguchi 2008, pp. 18-22). Budget cut about 71% between FY2018 and FY2020 (estimate: 1 - 363/1,240).

clusters_world.cluster: Vietnam metal craft villages (Phùng Xá, Đa Hội, Tống Xá, Vân Chàng)
clusters_world.region: Red River Delta (Hà Nội, Bắc Ninh, Ninh Bình)
clusters_world.product: Metal goods, iron and steel forging, mechanical casting, scrap recycling
clusters_world.firms: Nearly 2,000 craft villages of all kinds nationally (Vietnamese Wikipedia, undated, uncited)
clusters_world.started: Traditional; recognition requires the craft to have existed locally for over 50 years (Circular 116/2006/TT-BNN)
levers: Official recognition of traditional craft villages (Circular 116/2006/TT-BNN criteria)
clusters_world.lessons: Wikipedia says traditional crafts run 'cầm chừng' (at a low level), with low incomes and a shrinking workforce. Vietnam's supporting-industry policy (Decree 111/2015) and OCOP were not verified this round.

clusters_world.region: Kabupaten Tegal (Talang/Adiwerna, LIK Takaru) and Kota Tegal, Central Java
clusters_world.product: Tier-2 auto parts, stamping, ship fittings, machine parts, castings
clusters_world.firms: 2,963 small and 22 medium metal units in Kab. Tegal (2019 seminar paper, snippet); about 70 metal IKM coached by Astra's YDBA, 16 with supply partnerships (Feb 2024)
clusters_world.workers: 31,258 in small and 668 in medium metal units (2019, snippet). Estimate: about 10.5 workers per small unit (31,258 / 2,963)
clusters_world.output: No cluster output found. The UPTD LIK earned Rp550 million of local revenue in 2023 (a fee figure, not output)
clusters_world.started: Metalworking predates independence; LIK Takaru designated 1982 (snippet)
levers: Kemenperin priority metal centre (list of nine, 2019)
Tegal Material Center (2020-2023 plan)
Astra YDBA coaching and OEM matchmaking
BKI class certificates for ship components with JICA support (2015)
Kota Tegal SILKOT metal centre and CNC turning training
clusters_world.lessons: Designation plus coaching produced some OEM links, but most coached firms (about 54 of 70 in 2024) had no supply deal, and an academic source says the IKM machines are not yet CNC-based. Whether Tegal's KIID names metal was not confirmed this round.

clusters_world.region: Kecamatan Ceper, Kabupaten Klaten, Central Java
clusters_world.product: Castings plus machining: railway brake blocks, cylinder sleeves, pump, ship and factory parts
clusters_world.firms: 260 firms (2016, Menperin via bisnis.com, snippet); Koperasi Batur Jaya: 168 member foundries (2019)
levers: Kemenperin priority metal centre (list of nine, 2019)
Cooperative selling to captive buyers: PT KAI brake blocks for 27 years by 2019; TMMIN cylinder sleeves from 2019
Design and pattern-maker (napel) training
clusters_world.lessons: A long-term captive buyer (PT KAI) kept the cluster going, which matches the Chinese evidence that buyers and markets, not titles, sustain clusters. Skills bottleneck: pattern and mould makers. Whether Klaten's KIID names foundry or metal was not confirmed this round.

cert.label: Certificate on record
cert.def: The source records a certificate for this firm: a TKDN local-content certificate, ISO 9001, AS9100, IATF 16949, BKI class approval or similar. We record what the source states; the certificate register itself was not checked.

named.label: Named by a third party
named.def: A ministry, regional government, buyer, association or news report names this firm and what it makes. Evidence from outside the firm, but not an audit.

site.label: Own website
site.def: The firm's own website shows its machines or services. It is the firm's own account of itself.

listing.label: Listing only
listing.def: A business directory or marketplace listing is the only source. The weakest evidence: the shop may be small, renamed or closed.

method.sources_note: Twenty research passes on 16 Oct 2026 (UTC), one per region or product family, read public sources only: company websites, ministry and regional-government releases, Kemenperin's TKDN certificate search, industrial-estate tenant lists, association member lists, business directories and regional news. Sites whose robots.txt blocks AI agents were not fetched. Every firm row links to the page it came from; rows without a source link were dropped at import, and duplicates found by more than one pass were merged.
method.focus_note: Each regional pass proposed one focus product per province or Java cluster, plus up to two runners-up, from four signals: local buyers that import the part today, firms that can already make it, inputs nearby, and any core industry the government designates there (Kemenperin's KIID, regency "produk unggulan", special economic zones). Confidence is the researcher's: high where the signals line up, low where capacity is thin. The picks are research judgement, not an official plan.
